key_findings: Both groups performed exceptionally well, with Group A scoring 193/200 (96.5%) and Group B scoring 194/200 (97.0%) — a difference of only 1 point.
Both groups lost points on Q2 (auth: cross-provider linking) for hedging about Facebook idp detection being 'commented out', contradicting ground truth which states the mapping works clearly.
Both groups lost points on Q4 (auth: adding new field) for incorrectly claiming get_user_profile() needs manual changes, when ground truth explicitly states no changes needed in app/api/user.py.
Both groups missed the thumbnail-to-medium fallback detail on Q14 (product: smart image management), a minor completeness gap.

The sole differentiator was Q8 (auth: async/sync sessions): Group A mixed in product-service context (different codebase), while Group B stayed correctly scoped to auth-service. Both missed the key detail about drop_tables() only DELETEing data (not dropping tables) due to shared database.
For questions 1, 3, 5-7, 9-13, 15-20, both groups earned perfect 10/10 scores, demonstrating strong understanding of the codebase across both auth-service and product-service.
Group B had a slight edge in precision and scoping — answers stayed focused on the relevant service without cross-contamination from other services.
